These values go straight to the encoder on the controlled phone, whose ADB link is the bottleneck: a smaller picture, a lower frame rate or a lower bitrate means less delay and fewer hitches, at the cost of sharpness.

The quality level is all VNC has to say about the picture: it reaches the server as a number from 0 to 9 and only affects the encodings which compress lossily, while Raw sends the pixels untouched. The resolution is a request, not a setting - a server without ExtendedDesktopSize keeps its own screen and the session says so when that happens. There is nothing here for bitrate or frame rate: the host sends a new picture whenever its screen changes, and what that costs on the wire follows from the level. Both apply on the next connection.

GameStream has no clipboard message, so a copy has nowhere to go. This app opens a second connection to a VNC server on the same PC and carries nothing over it but clipboard text - video and input stay on GameStream. With this off, copied text is typed out as keystrokes instead.
